You're right to chase, and I'm sorry. Hal confirmed the NerdQaxe++ fault on October 12, and the approval that releases your label still isn't on the order. Nothing went out to you, so you haven't missed an email.

I've pinged JD and Georges now and they're on until 6pm ET today. Stay in the chat if you can and one of them will pick it up here; if you step away, the approval and the prepaid return label come to (email hidden)

The moment it's approved I open the return and send you the label myself.
that was also the response last time I asked. But ok

Fair point, and I won't dress it up. The difference today is that it's flagged while they're still on, not sitting in a queue.

What I can do right now: the return is ready to go on my side, reference Shop····, label to our Chattanooga warehouse. The second the approval lands I buy the label and post it here, no further chasing from you.

For the three weeks of waiting I've made you a code for your next order, HD-••••••, $25 off, yours alone, works on orders over $100.
Is this going to be handled as a repair or an exchange?

A replacement, not a repair. We don't repair units in the field: the faulty one comes back to our Chattanooga warehouse on our prepaid label, and a new NerdQaxe++ goes out to you at no cost once it's checked in.

If the same model isn't on the shelf when we get there, I'll offer you something of equivalent value instead and let you pick.

One thing I should ask, since it affects warranty cover: was the unit ever overclocked or modified?
It never even got the point of hashing. No power on

Understood, that's a clean DOA then, nothing you did to it. Warranty cover isn't in question.

So it's a straight replacement: our label out to you, your unit back to Chattanooga with Shop···· on the box, new unit out as soon as it's checked in.

Nothing else needed from you right now. I'll post the label here the moment the approval comes through.
